title.zh: 卷433 列傳二百二十 金国琛 黄淳熙 吴坤修 康国器 李鹤章弟：昭庆 吴毓兰
title.en: Volume 433 Biographies 220: Jin Guochen, Huang Chunxi, Wu Kunxiu, Kang Guoqi, Li Hezhang younger brother: Zhao Qing, Wu Yulan
title.raw: 卷433 列傳二百二十 金国琛 黄淳熙 吴坤修 康国器 李鹤章弟：昭庆 吴毓兰

sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__

translations.literal: Table of contents marker.
translations.idiomatic: Table of contents.

sentences.zh: 金國琛，字逸亭，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Jin Guochen, styled Yiting, was a native of Jiangyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guochen, whose style name was Yiting, was from Jiangyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，以諸生謁羅澤南於江西，使參軍事。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng era, as a licentiate he called on Luo Zeyuan in Jiangxi and was assigned to military staff duties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign he went to Jiangxi as a licentiate to seek out Luo Zeyuan and was put on his military staff.

sentences.zh: 每出戰，部伍嚴整，倉猝犯之，屹然不亂。

translations.literal: Whenever he took the field, his ranks were tightly ordered; if the enemy struck suddenly, they stood firm without breaking.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign his units kept strict formation, and even when the enemy hit them without warning they held their ground without disorder.

sentences.zh: 轉戰弋陽、廣信、武昌、黃州，累功擢知縣。

translations.literal: He fought at Yiyang, Guangxin, Wuchang, and Huangzhou, and through accumulated merit was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He fought through Yiyang, Guangxin, Wuchang, and Huangzhou, and for repeated merit was raised to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 七年，李續賓代澤南，使總理營務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Li Xubin replaced Zeyuan and had him oversee camp administration in general.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Li Xubin succeeded Zeyuan and put him in charge of overall camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 率師會襲湖口，克之。

translations.literal: He led troops in a joint assault on Hukou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He led his forces in a combined attack on Hukou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 進復彭澤小姑洑、泰坪關，擊退援賊，晉秩同知直隸州。

translations.literal: Advancing, he recovered Xiaogufu in Pengze and Taiping Pass, drove back relieving rebels, and was promoted in rank to subprefect of Zhili prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to retake Xiaogufu in Pengze and Taiping Pass, beat back the relieving rebels, and was promoted to subprefect of Zhili prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，從克九江，窺安徽，下太湖、潛山、桐城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed in the capture of Jiujiang, turned his gaze toward Anhui, and took Taihu, Qianshan, and Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took part in the capture of Jiujiang, then pressed into Anhui and seized Taihu, Qianshan, and Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 續賓戰歿三河，國琛與其弟續宜招集散亡，勞徠撫慰，重申紀律，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: When Xubin fell in battle at Sanhe, Guochen and his younger brother Xuyi gathered the scattered survivors, comforted and reassured them, reasserted discipline, and the army's strength revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Xubin was killed at Sanhe, Guochen and his younger brother Xuyi rallied the scattered troops, consoled and reassured them, restored discipline, and the army's fighting spirit returned.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，石達開犯湖南，圍寶慶。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan and besieged Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan and laid siege to Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 國琛從續宜赴援，毀田家渡賊壘，又敗賊賀家坳，斬悍賊胡德孝，賊走廣西，擢知府。

translations.literal: Guochen followed Xuyi to the relief, destroyed rebel stockades at Tianjiadu, defeated the rebels again at Hejia'ao, beheaded the fierce rebel Hu Dexiao, and when the rebels fled to Guangxi he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Guochen marched with Xuyi to relieve the siege, destroyed the rebel fort at Tianjiadu, routed them again at Hejia'ao, and slew the fierce rebel Hu Dexiao; when the rebels fled into Guangxi he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 其冬，胡林翼、曾國籓規皖，精兵猛將萃於潛山、太湖。

translations.literal: That winter Hu Linyi and Zeng Guofan planned the Anhui campaign, and crack troops and fierce generals gathered at Qianshan and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hu Linyi and Zeng Guofan laid plans for Anhui, concentrating elite troops and veteran commanders at Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成糾眾數十萬，結捻匪龔瞎子圍鮑超於小池驛，救兵迭失利。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng mustered several hundred thousand men, joined with Nian bandit Gong Xiazi, and besieged Bao Chao at Xiaochi Post; relief columns suffered defeat after defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng raised several hundred thousand men, allied with the Nian bandit Gong Xiazi, and penned Bao Chao in at Xiaochi Post, while one relief force after another was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 先是林翼以國琛行軍善規地勢，令率十四營冒雪趨天堂備援。

translations.literal: Earlier Linyi, knowing Guochen was skilled at reading terrain on the march, had ordered him to lead fourteen battalions through the snow toward Tiantang as a reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Linyi knew Guochen excelled at judging ground on campaign, he had sent him with fourteen battalions through the snow toward Tiantang to stand ready as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 至事急，乃出高橫嶺，屯仰天庵，俯視賊營，皆在目中。

translations.literal: When the crisis came he came out by Gaoheng Ridge and encamped at Yangtian'an, looking down so that every rebel camp lay within sight.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis broke he marched out by Gaoheng Ridge and camped at Yangtian'an, from which he could look down and see every rebel encampment spread below.

sentences.zh: 賊驟見旗幟，大驚。

translations.literal: The rebels suddenly saw his banners and were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suddenly caught sight of his banners and were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，賊乘霧登山來犯，國琛揮軍突起躪之，合山下軍奮擊，斬馘逾萬，乘勝克潛山、太湖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year the rebels used fog to climb the hill and attack; Guochen waved his army forward in a sudden charge and trampled them, joined the troops below in a fierce assault, slew more than ten thousand, and pressing the advantage took Qianshan and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year the rebels used the fog to climb the heights and attack; Guochen threw his men forward in a sudden charge and rode them down, then joined the force below in a furious assault that killed more than ten thousand; pressing the advantage he took Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 林翼疏陳：「非鮑軍之堅忍，不能久持；

translations.literal: Linyi memorialized: "Without Bao's army's steadfast endurance, the position could not have been held so long;
translations.idiomatic: Linyi wrote in a memorial: "Without the steadfast endurance of Bao's army the line could not have been held so long;

sentences.zh: 非國琛之出奇制勝，不能轉危為安。」

translations.literal: without Guochen's striking with the unexpected to seize victory, danger could not have been turned to safety."
translations.idiomatic: without Guochen's unexpected stroke that turned the battle, danger could not have been turned to safety."

sentences.zh: 論功，擢道員。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪復犯湖北，國琛馳援武昌，連復孝感、云夢，進攻德安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Cantonese rebels again invaded Hubei; Guochen rushed to relieve Wuchang, recovered Xiaogan and Yunmeng in succession, and advanced to attack De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Taiping rebels invaded Hubei again; Guochen hurried to relieve Wuchang, retook Xiaogan and Yunmeng in turn, and advanced on De'an.

sentences.zh: 賊酋馬融和死斗，卒以長圍克之，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Ma Ronghe fought to the death, but in the end a long siege took the city; he received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Ma Ronghe fought to the last, but in the end a prolonged siege brought the city down, and Guochen was given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋授湖北安襄鄖荊道，仍兼治軍。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed intendant of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit in Hubei while still commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed intendant of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit in Hubei while continuing to command troops.

sentences.zh: 樊城地沖要，商賈所集，督軍士筑土城，不煩民力，賴為保障。

translations.literal: Fancheng stood at a strategic crossroads where merchants gathered; he directed soldiers to build an earthen wall without troubling the populace for labor, and it served as a dependable defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fancheng lay at a vital junction where merchants gathered; he had his soldiers build an earthen wall without calling on civilian labor, and it became a reliable bulwark.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪西擾關中，命國琛率師赴援，以鄖西戒嚴，留未行。

translations.literal: At that time Nian bandits were raiding west into Guanzhong and he was ordered to lead troops to the relief, but because Yunxi was on alert he remained and did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian bandits were raiding west into Guanzhong he was ordered to lead troops to the relief, but Yunxi was placed on alert and he was kept from marching.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，馬融和以眾六萬圍南陽，國琛越境往援，力戰解城圍，拔出難民數萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Ma Ronghe with sixty thousand men besieged Nanyang; Guochen crossed the border to relieve it, fought hard to lift the siege, and rescued tens of thousands of refugees.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi Ma Ronghe besieged Nanyang with sixty thousand men; Guochen crossed into the neighboring province to relieve the city, fought fiercely to break the siege, and brought out tens of thousands of civilians.

sentences.zh: 巡撫嚴樹森忌之，劾其不遵調度，以同知降補。

translations.literal: Governor Yan Shusen envied him and impeached him for disobeying orders; he was demoted and reassigned as subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yan Shusen, jealous of him, impeached him for failing to follow orders, and he was demoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 二年，曾國籓調統義從營。

translations.literal: In the second year Zeng Guofan transferred him to command the Yicong Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zeng Guofan assigned him to command the Yicong Battalion.

sentences.zh: 擊賊徽州，屢捷於豹嶺、佛嶺、黃傋口、小溪。

translations.literal: Attacking rebels in Huizhou, he won repeated victories at Baoling, Foling, Huangzhangkou, and Xiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting rebels in Huizhou he won repeated victories at Baoling, Foling, Huangzhangkou, and Xiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 皖南肅清，復原官，補甘肅鞏秦階道。

translations.literal: When southern Anhui was pacified he was restored to his former rank and appointed to the Yong-Qin-Jie circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After southern Anhui was cleared he was restored to his former rank and appointed intendant of the Yong-Qin-Jie circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 以母老假歸。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged he took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave to go home because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，起復廣東督糧道，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was recalled to serve as grain superintendent of Guangdong and was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was recalled as grain superintendent of Guangdong and promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 國琛以儒生治軍十餘年，堅苦踔厲，號為名將。

translations.literal: Guochen, a scholar in command of troops for more than ten years, was steadfast, arduous, and bold, and was acclaimed as a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar who had led troops for more than ten years, Guochen was known for his grit and daring and was acclaimed as a famous general.

sentences.zh: 居官亦有政聲。

translations.literal: In civil office he also had a reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: As a civil official he likewise earned a reputation for sound governance.

sentences.zh: 黃淳熙，字子春，江西鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Chunxi, styled Zichun, was a native of Poyang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chunxi, whose style name was Zichun, was from Poyang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，湖南即用知縣，歷署綏寧、會同。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, he was assigned as magistrate in Hunan and successively acted as magistrate of Suining and Huitong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, was posted as magistrate in Hunan, and served in acting posts at Suining and Huitong.

sentences.zh: 剛直為時所忌，引疾閒居。

translations.literal: His blunt integrity made him disliked in his day, and he pleaded illness and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt integrity made him unpopular, and he pleaded illness and withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，巡撫駱秉章廉知其賢，使強起之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Governor Luo Bingzhang, knowing his worth, had him forcibly recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng Governor Luo Bingzhang, recognizing his talent, pressed him back into service.

sentences.zh: 七年，署湘鄉，有異政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he acted as magistrate of Xiangxiang and achieved notable administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served as acting magistrate of Xiangxiang and won notice for exceptional governance.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽方陷賊，移家於湘鄉。

translations.literal: Poyang had just fallen to rebels, so he moved his family to Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang had just fallen to the rebels, so he moved his family to Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓方起督浙江軍，辟參軍事，不就。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan was just taking command of the Zhejiang army and invited him to join the staff, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was just assuming command of the Zhejiang campaign and invited him onto his staff, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開犯湖南，秉章檄淳熙募勇千六百人防省城，時出剿賊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan; Bingzhang ordered Chunxi to raise sixteen hundred braves to defend the provincial capital and sent him out from time to time to suppress rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Shi Dakai invaded Hunan, Bingzhang ordered Chunxi to raise sixteen hundred militiamen to defend the provincial capital and sent him out repeatedly to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 達開由寶慶竄踞嶺東，分黨犯江華，淳熙破之於掛勾嶺，遂夜襲嶺東賊營，躡至江、藍，殲殪甚眾。

translations.literal: Dakai fled from Baoqing and seized the eastern passes; he sent detachments against Jianghua, and Chunxi defeated them at Guagou Ridge, then raided the rebel camp in the eastern passes by night, pursued them to Jiang and Lan, and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai broke out from Baoqing and seized the eastern passes, then sent detachments against Jianghua; Chunxi routed them at Guagou Ridge, launched a night attack on the rebel camp in the eastern passes, pursued them into Jiang and Lan counties, and slaughtered a great many.

sentences.zh: 進剿賊黨賴裕新，乘霧敗之，破杉木根、黃馬寨而還。

translations.literal: Advancing against the rebel band under Lai Yuxin, he used fog to defeat them, broke Shanmugen and Huangmazhai, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the rebel Lai Yuxin, used the fog to rout him, stormed Shanmugen and Huangmazhai, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 十年，達開黨眾四出，淳熙轉戰於永、道、綏、靖諸州，復宜章、桂陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Dakai's followers ranged widely; Chunxi fought through Yong, Dao, Sui, and Jing prefectures and recovered Yizhang and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Dakai's forces fanned out in every direction; Chunxi fought through Yong, Dao, Sui, and Jing and recovered Yizhang and Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 前后三十餘戰，皆捷，累擢知府，以道員記名。

translations.literal: In more than thirty battles before and after, all were victories; he was repeatedly promoted to prefect and was recorded by name for intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In more than thirty engagements he was victorious every time; he was repeatedly promoted to prefect and placed on the list for intendant.

sentences.zh: 所部曰果毅營，增至三千人。

translations.literal: His command was called the Guoyi Battalion and was increased to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: His unit, called the Guoyi Battalion, grew to three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章奉命赴四川督師，湘軍名將勁兵多從曾國籓、胡林翼，劉蓉薦淳熙兵精善戰，秉章遂以淳熙與劉岳昭從行。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang was ordered to Sichuan to command troops; many famous Hunan generals and crack soldiers followed Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi, but Liu Rong recommended Chunxi's troops as elite and skilled in battle, so Bingzhang took Chunxi and Liu Yuezhao with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang was ordered to Sichuan to take command, most of the Hunan army's star generals and crack troops had gone with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi; Liu Rong recommended Chunxi's force as elite and battle-hardened, so Bingzhang took Chunxi and Liu Yuezhao with him.

sentences.zh: 至荊州，岳昭復留，獨淳熙以所部當軍鋒。

translations.literal: At Jingzhou Yuezhao was again left behind, and Chunxi alone led his own troops at the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou Yuezhao was left behind again, and Chunxi alone led his men at the point of the army.

sentences.zh: 分道溯峽上，次萬縣，聞順慶被圍，率師赴援。

translations.literal: They split forces and went up the gorges, halted at Wanxian, heard that Shunqing was besieged, and led troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced up the gorges by separate routes, halted at Wanxian, and on hearing that Shunqing was besieged marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 五月，至，賊走定遠，追之，距定遠二十里，望賊屯城西南，連十餘里，城東北江水環繞，賊方造浮橋渡水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he arrived; the rebels fled to Dingyuan and he pursued. Twenty li from Dingyuan he saw rebel camps southwest of the city stretching more than ten li; northeast of the city the river wrapped around, and the rebels were building a pontoon bridge to cross the water.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived in the fifth month; the rebels withdrew to Dingyuan and he pursued. Twenty li from the city he saw their camps spread southwest of the walls for more than ten li; northeast of the city the river curved around them while they were building a pontoon bridge to cross.

sentences.zh: 淳熙分三路進，遇賊即前搏之，擲火焚其屯，賊大亂爭走，二十餘壘悉潰，擒斬數千。

translations.literal: Chunxi advanced in three columns, closed with the rebels wherever he met them, threw fire to burn their camps, and the rebels broke in great disorder and fled; more than twenty stockades collapsed entirely and several thousand were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi advanced in three columns, closing with the enemy wherever he met them, set fire to their camps, and sent them fleeing in chaos; more than twenty stockades were overrun and several thousand were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 殲首賊何國樑，解散脅從萬餘人。

translations.literal: He destroyed the chief rebel He Guoliang and released more than ten thousand coerced followers.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the rebel chief He Guoliang and released more than ten thousand coerced followers.

sentences.zh: 賊黨彭紹福率眾千餘屯東岸，收集潰賊，竄二郎場，淳熙銳進，欲一戰平之。

translations.literal: The rebel Peng Shaofu with more than a thousand men camped on the east bank, gathered routed rebels, and fled to Erlangchang; Chunxi pressed forward sharply, intending to settle it in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Peng Shaofu camped on the east bank with more than a thousand men, gathered the routed troops, and withdrew to Erlangchang; Chunxi pressed forward hard, hoping to finish them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 二郎場在山中，羊腸曲逕，通遂寧兩路，均為涪江阻。

translations.literal: Erlangchang lay in the mountains along winding goat paths; two roads led to Suining, both blocked by the Fu River.
translations.idiomatic: Erlangchang lay in the mountains along narrow winding paths; two roads led toward Suining, both cut off by the Fu River.

sentences.zh: 別賊硃甲眾數千由青岡壩至，四路設伏。

translations.literal: Another rebel force, Zhu Jia, with several thousand men came from Qinggangba and set ambushes on four roads.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel commander, Zhu Jia, arrived from Qinggangba with several thousand men and laid ambushes on four roads.

sentences.zh: 淳熙遣偵不見賊，五鼓師行，賊燕子窠，擊走之，逼二郎場。

translations.literal: Chunxi sent scouts but saw no rebels; at the fifth watch the army marched, the rebels were at Yanziwowo, he drove them off, and pressed on Erlangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi sent scouts but found no enemy; at the fifth watch his army marched, routed the rebels at Yanziwowo, and pressed on toward Erlangchang.

sentences.zh: 賊分兩路繞山麓上，淳熙知有伏，令諸營左右搜捕，自率中軍策應。

translations.literal: The rebels split into two columns and came around the foot of the hills; Chunxi knew there were ambushes and ordered the battalions to search left and right while he led the center in support.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came around the foothills in two columns; Chunxi sensed an ambush and ordered his battalions to search the flanks while he led the center in support.

sentences.zh: 兵分，伏賊起，遍布山岡。

translations.literal: As the troops dispersed, ambushing rebels rose and spread over the hill ridges.
translations.idiomatic: As his men spread out, hidden rebels sprang up all along the ridges.

sentences.zh: 官軍走田塍，泥深輒陷。

translations.literal: Government troops fled along the field paths; the mud was deep and men sank in it.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops fled along the field embankments, sinking deep into the mud.

sentences.zh: 淳熙率親卒拒戰，被圍，策馬突陣，陷淖中，棄馬，手刃十餘賊，中矛仆，擁至場，支解燔之。

translations.literal: Chunxi led his personal guard to resist, was surrounded, spurred his horse to break the formation, sank in the mire, abandoned his horse, killed more than ten rebels with his own hand, was struck by a spear and fell, was dragged to the field, dismembered, and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi led his personal guard in a stand, was surrounded, spurred his horse to break through, sank in the mire, abandoned his mount, and killed more than ten rebels with his own blade before a spear brought him down; the rebels dragged him to the field, dismembered him, and burned his body.

sentences.zh: 賊懾其軍勇猛，不復追，餘部整隊還，賊亦遁走。

translations.literal: The rebels feared his army's fierceness and did not pursue further; the remainder reformed ranks and withdrew, and the rebels also fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, awed by his army's ferocity, did not pursue; the survivors reformed and withdrew, and the rebels likewise fled.

sentences.zh: 淳熙雖戰歿，湘軍之威因之頓振。

translations.literal: Although Chunxi fell in battle, the prestige of the Hunan army was thereby suddenly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chunxi died in battle, the prestige of the Hunan army was suddenly restored.

sentences.zh: 詔贈布政使，賜恤，加贈內閣學士，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him provincial administration commissioner, bestowed condolence gifts, added posthumous grant of Grand Secretary of the Hall, and gave the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him provincial administration commissioner, granted mourning favors, added the posthumous rank of Grand Secretary, and gave him the posthumous title Zhongzhuang, "Loyal and Bold."

sentences.zh: 吳坤修，字竹莊，江西新建人。

translations.literal: Wu Kunxiu, styled Zhuzhuang, was a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kunxiu, whose style name was Zhuzhuang, was from Xinjian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 捐納從九，分發湖南。

translations.literal: By purchase he obtained the rank of subordinate ninth grade and was assigned to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased the rank of subordinate ninth grade and was posted to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年，賑湘陰水災，勤於事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he relieved the flood disaster in Xiangyin and was diligent in the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he directed flood relief in Xiangyin and worked with notable diligence.

sentences.zh: 從剿李沅發，以府經歷、縣丞補用。

translations.literal: He followed in the suppression of Li Yuanfa and was appointed in supplementary posts as prefectural registrar and assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing Li Yuanfa and was appointed in supplementary posts as prefectural registrar and assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪犯長沙，以守城功擢知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels attacked Changsha, he was promoted to magistrate for merit in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, when the Taiping rebels attacked Changsha, he was promoted to magistrate for his part in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓創立水師，坤修司軍械。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan founded the river navy, Kunxiu was in charge of ordnance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan founded the river navy, Kunxiu was put in charge of ordnance.

sentences.zh: 四年，水師攻九江，入鄱陽湖，為賊所阻不得出，令坤修單騎往南康，導往吳城、南昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the navy attacked Jiujiang and entered Poyang Lake but was blocked by rebels and could not get out; he ordered Kunxiu to ride alone to Nankang and guide the way to Wucheng and Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the fleet attacked Jiujiang and entered Poyang Lake but was trapped by the rebels; Zeng sent Kunxiu alone on horseback to Nankang to guide a route to Wucheng and Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 五年，率舟師防瑞豐。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he led the fleet to defend Ruifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he led the fleet to defend Ruifeng.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 既而武昌復陷，坤修從羅澤南援湖北，復咸寧、蒲圻、崇陽、通城，累擢同知，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon after Wuchang fell again; Kunxiu followed Luo Zeyuan to relieve Hubei, recovered Xianning, Puqi, Chongyang, and Tongcheng, was repeatedly promoted to subprefect, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell again he followed Luo Zeyuan to relieve Hubei, retook Xianning, Puqi, Chongyang, and Tongcheng, was repeatedly promoted to subprefect, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 進規武昌。

translations.literal: He advanced to plan the recovery of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to lay plans for recovering Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 六年，江西軍事不利，胡林翼令坤修領新募軍曰彪字營，會湘軍援江西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Jiangxi's military situation turned unfavorable; Hu Linyi had Kunxiu lead newly raised troops called the Biaozi Battalion to join Hunan forces in relieving Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Jiangxi's campaign went badly, Hu Linyi put Kunxiu in command of newly raised troops called the Biaozi Battalion to join the Hunan army in relieving Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 復新昌、上高。

translations.literal: He recovered Xinchang and Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Xinchang and Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 由新昌取道羅坊攻奉新，梯城而登，賊死守不能拔，乃先下安義、靖安，后萃軍奉新。

translations.literal: From Xinchang he took the road through Luofang to attack Fengxin, scaled the walls by ladder, but the rebels held firm and he could not take it; he therefore first reduced Anyi and Jing'an, then massed his army at Fengxin.
translations.idiomatic: From Xinchang he marched by Luofang to attack Fengxin, scaled the walls by ladder, but the defenders held out and he could not take the city; he therefore seized Anyi and Jing'an first, then concentrated his forces at Fengxin.

sentences.zh: 時江西餉絀，坤修傾家貲，并勸族里富人出銀米餉軍；

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxi's pay was exhausted; Kunxiu poured out his family wealth and also urged wealthy clansmen to contribute silver and grain to supply the army;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi's funds were exhausted at the time; Kunxiu spent his family fortune and persuaded wealthy kinsmen to contribute silver and grain for the troops;

sentences.zh: 又籌銀四萬兩解省垣，收集平江潰勇。

translations.literal: he also raised forty thousand taels of silver for the provincial capital and gathered routed braves from Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: he also raised forty thousand taels for the provincial capital and gathered the routed militia from Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 七年春，克奉新，累擢道員。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he took Fengxin and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he captured Fengxin and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋授廣東南韶連道，仍留軍，克瑞州。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed intendant of the Nan-Shao-Lian circuit in Guangdong but remained with the army and took Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed intendant of the Nan-Shao-Lian circuit in Guangdong but stayed with the army and captured Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，東鄉師潰，被劾褫職。

translations.literal: That winter the army was routed at Dongxiang and he was impeached and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his force was routed at Dongxiang; he was impeached and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 九年，駐師撫州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he stationed troops at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he encamped his troops at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫耆齡檄督辦撫、建、寧三屬團練，始立團防營，駐貴溪。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Governor Qiling ordered him to supervise militia training in the three districts of Fu, Jian, and Ning; he first established the Tuanfang Battalion and stationed it at Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Governor Qiling ordered him to oversee militia training in Fu, Jian, and Ning; he founded the Tuanfang Battalion and stationed it at Guixi.

sentences.zh: 移德興，出援徽州。

translations.literal: He moved to Dexing and went out to relieve Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Dexing and marched out to relieve Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，克建德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he took Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he captured Jiande.

sentences.zh: 秋，徽防軍潰，坤修方假歸，其弟修敳攝軍事，守嶺外郭村。

translations.literal: In autumn the Huizhou defense force collapsed; Kunxiu was on leave, and his younger brother Xiuyi took command, holding Guocun beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Huizhou defense force collapsed; Kunxiu was on leave, and his younger brother Xiuyi took command and held Guocun beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 調回江西，曾國籓令守湖口，而巡撫毓科檄援建昌。

translations.literal: He was transferred back to Jiangxi; Zeng Guofan ordered him to hold Hukou, but Governor Yuker ordered him to relieve Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to Jiangxi; Zeng Guofan ordered him to hold Hukou, but Governor Yuker ordered him to relieve Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 賊由金谿竄東鄉，坤修自撫州迎擊於鄧家埠，大破之。

translations.literal: Rebels fled from Jinxi into Dongxiang; Kunxiu marched from Fuzhou to meet them at Dengjiabu and routed them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels broke out from Jinxi into Dongxiang; Kunxiu marched from Fuzhou to intercept them at Dengjiabu and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 賊復出貴溪竄安仁，遏之不得渡河，乃竄德興、萬年，將擾景德鎮。

translations.literal: The rebels came out again from Guixi into Anren; he blocked them and they could not cross the river, so they fled into Dexing and Wannian, intending to harass Jingdezhen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke out from Guixi toward Anren; he blocked them from crossing the river, so they fled into Dexing and Wannian, threatening Jingdezhen.

sentences.zh: 坤修由饒州馳援景德，以固祁門大軍后路。

translations.literal: Kunxiu rushed from Raozhou to relieve Jingdezhen and secure the rear of the main army at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxiu hurried from Raozhou to relieve Jingdezhen and secure the rear of the main army at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 會賊由建德上犯，國籓令援湖口。

translations.literal: Just then rebels advanced up from Jiande, and Guofan ordered him to relieve Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Just then rebels advanced from Jiande, and Guofan ordered him to relieve Hukou.

sentences.zh: 坤修且戰且進，先賊至，城恃以完，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: Kunxiu fought as he advanced, reached the city before the rebels, and it was preserved intact; he received the nominal rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxiu fought his way forward, reached the city before the rebels, and saved it from capture; he was given the nominal rank of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李秀成自蘇州援江寧，分犯蕪湖，會軍擊卻之，又會克金保圩、高淳、溧水及溧陽、東壩各要隘，遣散降眾數萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Xiucheng came from Suzhou to relieve Jiangning and sent detachments against Wuhu; Kunxiu joined the army and drove them back, then took part in capturing Jinbaowei, Gaochun, Lishui, and the key passes at Liyang and Dongba, and released tens of thousands of surrendered followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Xiucheng marched from Suzhou to relieve Jiangning and sent detachments against Wuhu; Kunxiu joined the allied force and beat them back, then helped capture Jinbaowei, Gaochun, Lishui, and the key positions at Liyang and Dongba, and released tens of thousands of surrendered men.

sentences.zh: 三年，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the third year he received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江寧克復，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was recovered he was recorded by name for provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning was recovered he was placed on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，署徽寧池太廣道，授安徽按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he acted as intendant of the Hui-Ning-Chi-Tai-Guang circuit and was appointed Anhui provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he served as acting intendant of the Hui-Ning-Chi-Tai-Guang circuit and was appointed Anhui provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he acted as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as acting provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，巡撫英翰駐潁州，出境剿捻，坤修轉輸餉運，未嘗遲乏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Governor Yinghan was stationed at Yingzhou and went beyond the border to suppress Nian bandits; Kunxiu transported pay and supplies and was never late or short.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Governor Yinghan was at Yingzhou campaigning against the Nian beyond the border, Kunxiu handled supply transport and never fell behind or ran short.

sentences.zh: 七年，署巡撫，實授布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he acted as governor and was then appointed provincial administration commissioner in substantive rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served as acting governor and was then appointed provincial administration commissioner in substantive rank.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，請假回籍補終父母喪。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he asked leave to return home and complete mourning for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were suppressed he took leave to go home and complete the mourning period for his parents.

sentences.zh: 九年，回任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 巡撫英翰疏陳其戰功政績，賜恤，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Governor Yinghan memorialized his battle merit and administrative achievements; condolence gifts were granted and he was posthumously made Grand Secretary of the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yinghan memorialized his military and civil record; mourning favors were granted and he was posthumously made Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 康國器，初名以泰，字交修，廣東南海人。

translations.literal: Kang Guoqi, originally named Yitai, styled Jiaoxiu, was a native of Nanhai in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guoqi, originally named Yitai and styled Jiaoxiu, was from Nanhai in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 少為吏員。

translations.literal: In youth he was a minor clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a minor clerk.

sentences.zh: 道光末，從軍，以勞授江西贛縣桂源司巡檢。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang era he joined the army and, for merit, was appointed inspector of Guiyuan subdistrict in Ganxian, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daoguang reign he joined the army and, for his service, was appointed inspector of Guiyuan subdistrict in Ganxian, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，粵匪犯江西，土寇蜂起，國器募死士三百，贛南道周玉衡檄擊賊烏兜、良口，克萬安。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels invaded Jiangxi and local bandits rose everywhere, Guoqi raised three hundred dare-to-die men; the Gannan circuit intendant Zhou Yuheng ordered attacks on rebels at Wudou and Liangkou, and Wan'an was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, when the Taiping rebels invaded Jiangxi and local bandits rose on every side, Guoqi raised three hundred dare-to-die fighters; Circuit Intendant Zhou Yuheng of southern Gan ordered strikes on the rebels at Wudou and Liangkou, and Wan'an was captured.

sentences.zh: 造船三十艘，習水戰。

translations.literal: He built thirty boats and trained in naval combat.
translations.idiomatic: He built thirty boats and trained his men in river warfare.

sentences.zh: 六年，從克饒州，累擢知縣，署南城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he took part in capturing Raozhou, was repeatedly promoted to magistrate, and acted as magistrate of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he helped capture Raozhou, was repeatedly promoted to magistrate, and served as acting magistrate of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 石達開陷瑞、撫、臨、吉四郡，國器從克樟樹鎮，連戰瑞州、臨江、鉛山、安仁，擢同知。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai took the four prefectures of Rui, Fu, Lin, and Ji, Guoqi followed in the capture of Zhangshu Town, fought continuously at Ruizhou, Linjiang, Qianshan, and Anren, and was promoted to subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai seized the four prefectures of Rui, Fu, Lin, and Ji, Guoqi took part in capturing Zhangshu Town, fought through Ruizhou, Linjiang, Qianshan, and Anren, and was promoted to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 十一年，廣東巡撫耆齡檄剿陽山賊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Guangdong Governor Qiling ordered him to suppress rebels in Yangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guangdong Governor Qiling ordered him to suppress the rebels in Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 賊踞藍山，地阻絕，負隅十餘年。

translations.literal: The rebels held Lanshan; the terrain was inaccessible, and they had held out in a corner for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Lanshan, where the terrain was nearly impassable, and had defied the government there for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 國器緣崖歷磵出賊后，破石柵九，奪砲臺，毀其老巢。

translations.literal: Guoqi climbed cliffs and crossed streams to come up behind the rebels, broke nine stone palisades, seized artillery positions, and destroyed their main lair.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi climbed the cliffs and crossed the streams to get behind the rebels, stormed nine stone palisades, seized their batteries, and destroyed their main stronghold.

sentences.zh: 遣子熊飛單騎說降劇賊練四虎，其魁梁柱走豬頭寨，穴山攻獲之。

translations.literal: He sent his son Xiongfei alone on horseback to persuade the fierce rebel Lian Sihu to surrender; the chieftain Liang Zhu fled to Zhutou Stockade, which was taken by tunneling into the hill.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Xiongfei alone on horseback to persuade the fierce rebel Lian Sihu to surrender; the chieftain Liang Zhu fled to Zhutou Stockade, which Guoqi took by mining into the hill.

sentences.zh: 進軍赫巖，擒賊渠周裕等。

translations.literal: Advancing to Heyan, he captured rebel leaders including Zhou Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Heyan and captured the rebel leaders Zhou Yu and others.

sentences.zh: 藍山平，擢知府。

translations.literal: When Lanshan was pacified he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Lanshan was pacified he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，援浙，從蔣益澧圍湯溪，明年春，克之，擢道員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he went to relieve Zhejiang, followed Jiang Yili in besieging Tangxi, and took it the next spring; he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he marched to relieve Zhejiang, joined Jiang Yili in besieging Tangxi, and captured it the following spring; he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，克餘杭，功最多，授福建延建邵道，始專統一軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he took Yuhang with the greatest merit, was appointed intendant of the Yan-Jian-Shao circuit in Fujian, and for the first time commanded an army of his own.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he captured Yuhang with the greatest share of the credit, was appointed intendant of the Yan-Jian-Shao circuit in Fujian, and for the first time held sole command of an army.

sentences.zh: 粵匪汪海洋犯閩，陷武平、永平，李世賢踞漳州、龍巖與之合，旁郡縣多沒於賊。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebel Wang Haiyang invaded Fujian, took Wuping and Yongping, and Li Shixian held Zhangzhou and Longyan in alliance with him; many neighboring prefectures and counties fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebel Wang Haiyang invaded Fujian, seized Wuping and Yongping, and Li Shixian held Zhangzhou and Longyan in league with him; many neighboring districts fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠議三路進兵，國器自請當龍巖。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang planned a three-route advance, and Guoqi volunteered to take Longyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang planned a three-pronged advance, and Guoqi volunteered to take the Longyan front.

sentences.zh: 進軍雁石，令熊飛壁鐵石洋，三戰薄城下，破其眾數萬，并敗古田援賊。

translations.literal: He advanced to Yanshi, ordered Xiongfei to fortify Tieshiyang, fought three battles under the city walls, routed tens of thousands of the enemy, and also defeated relieving rebels from Gutian.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Yanshi and ordered Xiongfei to hold Tieshiyang; after three battles below the walls he routed tens of thousands of the enemy and also beat back the relieving force from Gutian.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遂克龍巖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he took Longyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he captured Longyan.

sentences.zh: 賊走永定，分踞苦竹、奎洋，勢猶熾。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Yongding and held Kuchu and Kuiyang in separate detachments; their power was still fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew to Yongding and held Kuchu and Kuiyang in separate positions; their strength was still formidable.

sentences.zh: 國器進擊苦竹，乘夜大霧，火賊營，破二十餘壘。

translations.literal: Guoqi advanced against Kuchu; in a heavy night fog he set fire to the rebel camps and broke more than twenty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi advanced on Kuchu; under cover of a thick night fog he burned the rebel camps and overran more than twenty stockades.

sentences.zh: 海洋以悍黨來援，敗之於東阬，又敗之大溪，乃竄廣東大浦境。

translations.literal: Haiyang came with fierce followers to relieve them; Guoqi defeated them at Dongkeng and again at Daxi, and they fled into the Dapu region of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang came with his toughest fighters to relieve them; Guoqi routed them at Dongkeng and again at Daxi, and they fled into the Dapu region of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，海洋復犯永定，國器馳毀羅灘橋；

translations.literal: Before long Haiyang invaded Yongding again; Guoqi hurried to destroy the Luotan Bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Haiyang invaded Yongding again; Guoqi hurried to destroy the Luotan Bridge;

sentences.zh: 賊分七路來撲，海洋自陣獅龍嶺，所部皆死黨，旗幟遍巖谷。

translations.literal: the rebels came in seven columns to attack, and Haiyang himself took position at Shilong Ridge; his men were all sworn diehards, and their banners filled the ravines and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: the rebels came at him in seven columns while Haiyang himself held Shilong Ridge; his men were all sworn diehards, and their banners filled the ravines and valleys.

sentences.zh: 國器曰：「賊精銳盡萃於此，若摧之，餘眾必奔。」

translations.literal: Guoqi said: "The rebels' elite are all gathered here; if we break them, the rest will surely flee."
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi said: "The enemy's best troops are all gathered here; if we break them, the rest will surely run."

sentences.zh: 乃堅壁深溝，伺怠出擊。

translations.literal: He therefore strengthened his walls and dug deep trenches, waited until they slackened, and then struck.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore strengthened his defenses and dug deep trenches, waited until the enemy slackened, and then struck.

sentences.zh: 先破其伏，分道猛進，斬馘數千，盡獲其軍實，海洋跳而免。

translations.literal: He first broke their ambush, advanced fiercely by separate routes, killed several thousand, captured all their military stores, and Haiyang leaped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He first broke their ambush, then advanced fiercely on several routes, killing several thousand and capturing all their stores; Haiyang leaped away and escaped.

sentences.zh: 時漳州亦下，李世賢西遁，遇國器於塔下，縱兵擊之，降其眾二萬人。

translations.literal: By then Zhangzhou had also fallen; Li Shixian fled west, met Guoqi below the pagoda, was attacked at full force, and twenty thousand of his men surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhangzhou had also fallen; Li Shixian fled west, met Guoqi below the pagoda, was attacked at full strength, and twenty thousand of his men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 海洋走廣東，踞鎮平。

translations.literal: Haiyang fled to Guangdong and held Zhenping.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang fled into Guangdong and held Zhenping.

sentences.zh: 國器進壁鎮平東南高思塘，分軍扼程官埠，賊數來犯，卻之。

translations.literal: Guoqi advanced and fortified Gaositang southeast of Zhenping, detached troops to hold Chengguanbu, and repelled repeated rebel attacks.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi advanced and fortified Gaositang southeast of Zhenping, detached troops to hold Chengguanbu, and beat back repeated rebel attacks.

sentences.zh: 國器知海洋將襲高思而虛攻程官埠，乃戒程官軍勿為動，設伏兩山間。

translations.literal: Guoqi knew Haiyang would strike Gaosi while making a feint at Chengguanbu; he warned the Chengguan force not to move and set ambushes between the two hills.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi knew Haiyang would strike Gaosi while feinting at Chengguanbu; he ordered the Chengguan force to hold still and laid ambushes between the two hills.

sentences.zh: 海洋果率悍黨來撲，誘入，伏突起，槍斃其梟汪大力、黃十四，海洋傷腕，陣斃及墮巖磵死者無數。

translations.literal: Haiyang indeed led fierce followers in an assault, was lured in, and the ambush rose; gunfire killed his chiefs Wang Dali and Huang Shisi, Haiyang was wounded in the wrist, and countless were killed in battle or fell from cliffs and streams.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang did lead his toughest fighters in an assault, was lured in, and the ambush rose; gunfire killed his chiefs Wang Dali and Huang Shisi, Haiyang was wounded in the wrist, and countless rebels were killed in battle or fell from the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 胡瞎子攻程官，亦敗走。

translations.literal: Hu Xiazi attacked Chengguan and was also beaten and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiazi attacked Chengguan and was likewise routed.

sentences.zh: 尋克鎮平。

translations.literal: Soon after Zhenping was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenping was captured soon after.

sentences.zh: 十二月，會諸軍擊賊嘉應，海洋伏誅，餘孽悉平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the allied armies struck the rebels at Jiaying; Haiyang was executed by ambush, and the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the allied armies struck the rebels at Jiaying; Haiyang was killed in an ambush, and the remaining rebels were all suppressed.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷廣西布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十年，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，內召，以疾歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned to the capital but returned home because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned to the capital but went home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Guangxu he died.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠疏陳戰績，請恤，格於吏議，特詔允之。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang memorialized his battle record and requested mourning favors; the Board of Civil Office blocked it, but a special edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang memorialized his battle record and requested mourning favors; the Board of Civil Office blocked the request, but a special edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 國器治軍能以少擊眾，常傷足而跛，軍中號康拐子，悍賊皆畏之。

translations.literal: Guoqi commanded troops able to strike many with few; he was often lame from a foot wound and was called Lame Kang in the army; fierce rebels all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi could defeat larger forces with smaller ones; lame from a foot wound, he was called Lame Kang in the army, and fierce rebels all feared him.

sentences.zh: 子熊飛，積功至浙江候補道，勇而有謀，常為軍鋒。

translations.literal: His son Xiongfei, through accumulated merit, reached the rank of expectant circuit intendant in Zhejiang; he was brave and resourceful and often led the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiongfei rose through merit to expectant circuit intendant in Zhejiang; brave and resourceful, he often led the van of the army.

sentences.zh: 國器數獲奇捷，實資其力云。

translations.literal: Guoqi won many extraordinary victories, and in truth owed them to his son's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi's many extraordinary victories owed much to his son's strength.

sentences.zh: 李鶴章，字季荃，安徽合肥人，大學士鴻章弟。

translations.literal: Li Hezhang, styled Jiquan, was a native of Hefei in Anhui and younger brother of Grand Secretary Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hezhang, whose style name was Jiquan, was from Hefei in Anhui and was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 從父兄治本籍團練，屢出戰有功，以州同用。

translations.literal: He followed his father and elder brother in organizing local militia in his native place, fought repeatedly with merit, and was appointed subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father and elder brother in organizing local militia at home, fought repeatedly with distinction, and was appointed subprefect.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，從克菱湖賊壘，復安慶，擢知縣，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he took part in capturing the rebel stockade at Linghu and recovering Anqing, was promoted to magistrate, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he helped capture the rebel stockade at Linghu and recover Anqing, was promoted to magistrate, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從鴻章援江蘇，常率親兵佐督戰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Hongzhang to relieve Jiangsu and often led personal troops to assist in directing battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Hongzhang to relieve Jiangsu and often led his personal guard in the field.

sentences.zh: 北新涇、四江口諸役，功皆最。

translations.literal: At Beixinjing, Sikoujiang, and other engagements his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: At Beixinjing, Sikoujiang, and other engagements his merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 又攻枝福山、許浦海口賊壘，招降常熟踞賊錢森仁。

translations.literal: He also attacked rebel stockades at Zhifushan and the Xu Pu estuary and persuaded Qian Senren, the rebel holding Changshu, to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also stormed rebel stockades at Zhifushan and the Xu Pu estuary and persuaded Qian Senren, the rebel holding Changshu, to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鴻章引嫌，奏捷不敘其勞，特旨詢問，命一體議敘，以知州用，加四品銜。

translations.literal: Hongzhang declined favoritism and in reporting victory did not record his brother's merit; a special edict inquired and ordered equal consideration of rewards, appointing him prefect with added fourth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang, avoiding favoritism, omitted his brother's merit from the victory report; a special edict inquired into the matter and ordered equal reward, appointing Hezhang prefect with added fourth-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年，會克太倉，規蘇州。

translations.literal: In the second year he joined in taking Taicang and laid plans for Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined in capturing Taicang and laid plans for Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 分諸軍為兩路，其進昆山一路，以程學啟為總統；

translations.literal: The armies were divided into two routes; the route advancing on Kunshan was placed under Cheng Xueqi as supreme commander;
translations.idiomatic: The armies were divided into two routes; the column advancing on Kunshan was placed under Cheng Xueqi as supreme commander;

sentences.zh: 由常熟進江陰者，鶴章督之。

translations.literal: the route from Changshu toward Jiangyin was directed by Hezhang.
translations.idiomatic: the column from Changshu toward Jiangyin was directed by Hezhang.

sentences.zh: 迭戰於常熟之王莊，江陰之南漍、北漍、顧山，毀賊壘，破援賊，會克江陰，擢知府。

translations.literal: He fought repeatedly at Wangzhuang in Changshu, Nanhan, Beihan, and Gushan in Jiangyin, destroyed rebel stockades, broke relieving rebels, joined in taking Jiangyin, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He fought repeatedly at Wangzhuang in Changshu and at Nanhan, Beihan, and Gushan in Jiangyin, destroyed rebel stockades, routed relieving forces, helped capture Jiangyin, and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 進攻無錫，踞賊黃子隆死守，李秀成屢來援；

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Wuxi; the holding rebel Huang Zilong defended to the death, and Li Xiucheng came repeatedly to relieve;
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Wuxi, where the rebel Huang Zilong held the city to the death while Li Xiucheng came repeatedly to relieve it;

sentences.zh: 及蘇州既克，潰賊亦麕聚，鶴章督水陸諸軍力戰克之，以道員記名簡放。

translations.literal: when Suzhou had been taken, routed rebels also gathered there; Hezhang directed land and naval forces in hard fighting and took the city, and was recorded by name for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: after Suzhou fell, routed rebels also massed there; Hezhang directed the land and naval forces in fierce fighting and took the city, and was placed on the list for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉鶴章：「能與兄同心戮力，為國宣勤。

translations.literal: An edict praised Hezhang: "Able to join his elder brother in one heart and united effort, proclaiming diligence for the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Hezhang: "He has joined his elder brother in loyal common effort and served the state with zeal.

sentences.zh: 此次未行破格之獎，為鴻章功不自私，俾得報勞將士，鼓舞眾心。

translations.literal: On this occasion no extraordinary reward was given, so that Hongzhang's merit might not be selfish and he could repay the labor of officers and soldiers and inspire all hearts.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion no extraordinary reward was given, so that Hongzhang's merit would not appear self-serving and he could reward his officers and soldiers and lift the army's morale.

sentences.zh: 指日常州、金陵次第奏捷，克成全功，更當與郭松林、劉銘傳等同膺懋賞。」

translations.literal: It is expected that when victories are reported in turn at Changzhou and Jinling and the great enterprise is completed, he should share rich rewards with Guo Songlin, Liu Mingchuan, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When victories follow at Changzhou and Jinling and the great enterprise is completed, he should share rich rewards with Guo Songlin, Liu Mingchuan, and the like.

sentences.zh: 鶴章進趨常州，與劉銘傳會攻，破援賊，解奔牛之圍。

translations.literal: Hezhang advanced on Changzhou, joined Liu Mingchuan in the assault, broke relieving rebels, and lifted the siege of Benniu.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhang advanced on Changzhou, joined Liu Mingchuan in the assault, routed the relieving rebels, and lifted the siege of Benniu.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，克常州，賜黃馬褂，授甘肅甘涼道。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he took Changzhou, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and was appointed intendant of the Gan-Liang circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he captured Changzhou, received the yellow riding jacket, and was appointed intendant of the Gan-Liang circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，曾國籓調其軍赴湖北。

translations.literal: That winter Zeng Guofan transferred his army to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zeng Guofan transferred his army to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 四年，以甘肅回亂棘，命赴本任，鶴章以傷發未行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because the Muslim rebellion in Gansu was acute, he was ordered to take up his post, but Hezhang's old wounds flared and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, with the Muslim rebellion in Gansu growing acute, he was ordered to take up his post, but Hezhang's old wounds flared and he did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋疾甚，國籓為奏請開缺，留襄營務。

translations.literal: Soon his illness grew severe; Guofan memorialized to have his post left vacant and kept him to assist with camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His illness soon grew severe; Guofan memorialized to leave his post vacant and kept him to assist with camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 未久，乞病歸，遂不出。

translations.literal: Before long he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home, and thereafter did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took sick leave and went home, and never held office again.

sentences.zh: 以捐助山西賑金，加二品銜。

translations.literal: For contributing to Shanxi famine relief he received added second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: For contributing to Shanxi famine relief he received added second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he died at home.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃疏陳：「李鴻章平江蘇，鶴章與程學啟各分統一路。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan memorialized: "When Li Hongzhang pacified Jiangsu, Hezhang and Cheng Xueqi each commanded a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan memorialized: "When Li Hongzhang pacified Jiangsu, Hezhang and Cheng Xueqi each commanded a separate column.

sentences.zh: 請將戰績宣付史館，於立功地建專祠。」

translations.literal: I request that his battle record be sent to the Historiography Institute and that a dedicated shrine be built at the place of his merit."
translations.idiomatic: I request that his battle record be sent to the Historiography Institute and that a dedicated shrine be built where he earned his merit."

sentences.zh: 允之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 子經羲，官至云貴總督。

translations.literal: His son Jingyi rose to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyi rose to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 弟昭慶，初從曾國籓軍，淮軍既立，國籓留五營，令昭慶領之，駐防無為、廬江。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhaoqing first followed Zeng Guofan's army; when the Huai army was established, Guofan retained five battalions and had Zhaoqing lead them, garrisoning Wuwei and Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhaoqing first served under Zeng Guofan; when the Huai army was formed, Guofan kept five battalions under Zhaoqing's command, garrisoning Wuwei and Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從鴻章至上海，解常熟圍，克嘉興、常州，皆在事有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Hongzhang to Shanghai, lifted the siege of Changshu, and took Jiaxing and Changzhou, serving with merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Hongzhang to Shanghai, helped lift the siege of Changshu, and took part in capturing Jiaxing and Changzhou with merit in each.

sentences.zh: 四年，國籓督師剿捻匪，昭慶總理營務，統武毅、忠樸等軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Guofan commanded troops against Nian bandits; Zhaoqing oversaw camp affairs and commanded the Wuyi, Zhongpu, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Guofan commanded the campaign against the Nian, Zhaoqing oversaw camp affairs and commanded the Wuyi, Zhongpu, and other armies.

sentences.zh: 及鴻章代國籓，令赴前敵擊賊，馳逐鄂、皖、東、豫之間，累擢至記名鹽運使。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang replaced Guofan he was ordered to the front to strike rebels, chased them between Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan, and was repeatedly promoted to expectant salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhang replaced Guofan he was sent to the front, pursued the rebels across Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan, and was repeatedly promoted to expectant salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 捻匪平，留防江、淮。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified he remained to garrison the Yangzi and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian were suppressed he remained to garrison the Yangzi and Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died and was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died and was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 吳毓蘭，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Wu Yulan was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yulan was from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，粵、捻合擾皖北，毓蘭以從九品偕兄毓芬集團練助剿鳳、潁間，從解壽州圍，擢縣丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese and Nian rebels jointly ravaged northern Anhui, Yulan, holding the rank of subordinate ninth grade, joined his elder brother Yufen in gathering militia to assist suppression between Fengyang and Yingzhou, took part in lifting the siege of Shouzhou, and was promoted to assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, when Taiping and Nian rebels jointly ravaged northern Anhui, Yulan, a subordinate ninth-grade officer, joined his elder brother Yufen in raising militia to fight between Fengyang and Yingzhou, helped lift the siege of Shouzhou, and was promoted to assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率師援上海，毓蘭從軍東下，克柘林、奉賢、南匯、川沙、青浦、金山，皆與有功，擢知縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang led troops to relieve Shanghai; Yulan followed the army east, took Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, Qingpu, and Jinshan, sharing merit in all, and was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Li Hongzhang marched east to relieve Shanghai, Yulan followed the army and helped capture Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, Qingpu, and Jinshan; for his share in these victories he was promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 二年，克嘉定，解北新涇、四江口之圍，加同知銜，領華字副營。

translations.literal: In the second year he took Jiading, lifted the sieges at Beixinjing and Sikoujiang, received added subprefect rank, and commanded the Huazi Auxiliary Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he captured Jiading, helped lift the sieges at Beixinjing and Sikoujiang, received added subprefect rank, and took command of the Huazi Auxiliary Battalion.

sentences.zh: 擊賊吳江八斥、牛尾墩、同里等處，進克平望、黎里，調守嘉善。

translations.literal: He struck rebels at Bachikou, Niuweidun, and Tongli in Wujiang, advanced to take Pingwang and Lili, and was transferred to garrison Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought rebels at Bachikou, Niuweidun, and Tongli in Wujiang, advanced to capture Pingwang and Lili, and was transferred to garrison Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 三年，率所部從總兵程學啟攻嘉興，戰於合歡橋。

translations.literal: In the third year he led his command with Major-General Cheng Xueqi to attack Jiaxing and fought at Hehuan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he led his troops with Major-General Cheng Xueqi to attack Jiaxing and fought at Hehuan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 毓蘭率槍船冒險渡河，先破賊卡，繞出賊營后，立拔之。

translations.literal: Yulan led gunboats across the river at risk, first broke a rebel barrier, swung around behind the rebel camp, and took it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yulan led gunboats across the river under fire, stormed a rebel barrier first, swung around behind the camp, and took it at once.

sentences.zh: 進抵城下，賊以巨砲拒河口，學啟被傷，毓蘭率先鋒攻益厲，掘河口架橋濟師，晝夜環攻，轟陷城垣百餘丈。

translations.literal: Advancing to the city, the rebels used great guns to block the river mouth; Xueqi was wounded, and Yulan led the vanguard in fiercer assault, dug at the river mouth and threw bridges to ferry troops, attacked day and night in encirclement, and blasted more than a hundred zhang of wall.
translations.idiomatic: At the city walls the rebels used heavy guns to block the river mouth; when Xueqi was wounded Yulan led the vanguard in a fiercer assault, dug at the river mouth and threw bridges across, and attacked night and day until more than a hundred zhang of wall were breached.

sentences.zh: 賊死抗不下，賊酋黃文金自湖州來援，力擊走之，遂克嘉興。

translations.literal: The rebels resisted to the death and would not yield; the rebel chief Huang Wensui came from Huzhou to relieve them, was driven off by hard fighting, and Jiaxing was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders fought to the death; when the rebel chief Huang Wensui came from Huzhou to relieve them Yulan beat him back and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 毓蘭緣梯先登，擢直隸州知州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Yulan was first up the ladders, was promoted to magistrate of Zhili prefecture, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Yulan was first up the ladders, was promoted to magistrate of Zhili prefecture, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調守溧陽，降賊屯城中，勢岌岌，突有金壇賊至，毓蘭與兄毓芬議乘賊初至破之，設伏以誘。

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison Liyang, with surrendered rebels encamped in the city and the situation precarious, rebels from Jintan suddenly arrived; Yulan and his elder brother Yufen planned to strike while they were newly arrived and set an ambush to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to garrison Liyang, with surrendered rebels encamped in the city and the situation precarious, rebels from Jintan suddenly appeared; Yulan and his brother Yufen planned to strike before they could settle in and laid an ambush to lure them.

sentences.zh: 賊敗走烏鴉嶺，毓蘭與毓芬兩路夾擊，擒斬無算。

translations.literal: The rebels were defeated and fled to Wuyaling; Yulan and Yufen struck from two routes and captured or killed beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed toward Wuyaling; Yulan and Yufen struck from two directions and killed or captured beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 窮追至建平境，陣斬賊目林得英、黃有才，擒黃金龍。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the border of Jianping, they killed in battle the rebel officers Lin Deying and Huang Youcai and captured Huang Jinlong.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing into Jianping territory, they killed the rebel officers Lin Deying and Huang Youcai in battle and captured Huang Jinlong.

sentences.zh: 溧陽既定，調守長興。

translations.literal: When Liyang was secured he was transferred to garrison Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Liyang was secured he was transferred to garrison Changxing.

sentences.zh: 時大軍已破湖州，毓蘭偵賊將竄泗安鎮，與毓芬夜率健卒八百冒雨疾走，潛渡觀音橋，賊不意兵至，棄糧械而走。

translations.literal: The main army had already taken Huzhou; Yulan learned the rebels would flee to Si'an Town, and with Yufen led eight hundred picked men by night through the rain in a forced march, crossed Guanyin Bridge in secret, and the rebels, not expecting troops, abandoned grain and weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had already taken Huzhou; learning the rebels would flee toward Si'an Town, Yulan and Yufen led eight hundred picked men through the rain on a night march, crossed Guanyin Bridge in secret, and caught the enemy unprepared so they abandoned their supplies and fled.

sentences.zh: 追至泗安，降者數千，敘功擢知府。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Si'an, several thousand surrendered; for merit he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to Si'an, where several thousand surrendered, and for his merit he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 四年，調守揚州，移廬州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to garrison Yangzhou and then moved to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was posted to garrison Yangzhou and then transferred to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，回屯揚州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he returned to encamp at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to encamp at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 追論平浙西功，以道員選用。

translations.literal: His merit in pacifying western Zhejiang was reviewed afterward and he was selected for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: His role in pacifying western Zhejiang was reviewed afterward and he was selected for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 六年，捻匪賴文光敗竄至揚州，為毓蘭所獲，以道員記名簡放。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Nian bandit Lai Wenguang, defeated and fleeing, reached Yangzhou and was captured by Yulan; he was recorded by name for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Nian leader Lai Wenguang, beaten and fleeing, reached Yangzhou and was captured by Yulan; he was placed on the list for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，尋加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he soon received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he soon received the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，李鴻章調充海防營務處，筦天津機器局。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Li Hongzhang transferred him to the coastal defense camp administration office and put him in charge of the Tianjin Machine Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Li Hongzhang assigned him to the coastal defense camp administration and put him in charge of the Tianjin Machine Works.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，授天津河間兵備道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was appointed military defense intendant of Tianjin and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was appointed military defense intendant of Tianjin and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 濱海多盜，毓蘭按名捕置諸法。

translations.literal: The coast had many bandits; Yulan arrested them by name and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were numerous along the coast; Yulan hunted them down by name and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 修南運河、子牙河堤，及千里堤灣，靜海、軍糧城河道，興水利。

translations.literal: He repaired the South Canal and the dikes of the Ziya River, the Qianli Dike bend, and the waterways of Jinghai and Junliangcheng, promoting water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the South Canal and the Ziya River dikes, the Qianli Dike bend, and the waterways at Jinghai and Junliangcheng, promoting irrigation and flood control.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，優恤，附祀曾國籓天津專祠，揚州建專祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; generous mourning favors were granted, he was given ancillary worship in Zeng Guofan's dedicated shrine at Tianjin, and a dedicated shrine was built for him at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died; generous mourning favors were granted, he was given a place in Zeng Guofan's dedicated shrine at Tianjin, and a dedicated shrine was built for him at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 論曰：金國琛為羅、李舊部。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Jin Guochen was of the old following of Luo and Li.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Jin Guochen belonged to the old following of Luo Zeyuan and Li Xubin.

sentences.zh: 黃淳熙后起，獨立一幟，雖非楚籍，并為湘軍名將。

translations.literal: Huang Chunxi rose later and flew his own banner; though not a native of Chu, both were famed generals of the Hunan army.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chunxi rose later and commanded a force of his own; though not a Hunan native, both were acclaimed generals of the Hunan army.

sentences.zh: 淳熙戰勝殞身，國琛遭忌鎩羽，皆未盡其才。

translations.literal: Chunxi won battles and fell in the field; Guochen met jealousy and had his wings clipped; none fully used their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi won his battles but died in the field; Guochen met jealousy and was cut down in his career; neither fully realized his abilities.

sentences.zh: 吳坤修、康國器起於令尉，功施爛然。

translations.literal: Wu Kunxiu and Kang Guoqi rose from minor local posts, and their achievements shone brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kunxiu and Kang Guoqi rose from minor local posts, and their achievements shone brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 李鶴章才績出眾，堪膺大用，后竟不出。

translations.literal: Li Hezhang's talent and record were outstanding and fit for great employment, yet in the end he did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hezhang's talent and record were outstanding and fit for high office, yet in the end he never returned to service.

sentences.zh: 吳毓蘭以擒獲巨憝顯名。

translations.literal: Wu Yulan won fame for capturing a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yulan won fame for capturing a great rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 功名之際，遭際固難測哉！

translations.literal: At the juncture of fame and achievement, how hard fortune is to foresee!
translations.idiomatic: At the turning point of fame and achievement, how impossible fortune is to foresee!
